newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lively Bunds set for gains but trade seen thin.
newsitem.headline: Lively Bunds set for gains but trade seen thin.

text.p: Prices on German Bunds and futures jumped higher on Friday, pulled up after short-covering boosted U.S. Treasuries overnight.
Traders said volumes were expected to be low in the German market after Thursday's Ascension Day holiday and with no significant domestic or international data on the cards.

But they said that with the U.S. market reacting well to comments from Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan, who said he expected U.S. growth to slow later this year, Bunds were also likely to aspire to gains this session.
By 0640 the June DTB Bund futures was already trading 38 basis points higher on the day at 102.09, having conquered psychological resistance at 102.00 in the first few minutes of trade.

"The market is in a very squeezy mood this morning," said Norman Beauchamp, head of derivatives at Cooperative Bank in London. "We're up 40 ticks already and it looks like we're going to squeeze higher."
The next technical targets for the June contract lay at 102.18, where the market plotted a high back on March 11, and then at 102.46, the old March 5 high.
Analysts said the market was well supported by German fundamentals and was getting a good leg up from the U.S. market, but had little news to focus on before the weekend and could be vulnerable.
"I'm a bit suspicious of this move," said Beauchamp. "I'm not saying I'd go short, but I'll probably be staying on the sidelines."

In the cash market, Bunds and T-notes continued to battle it out on spreads, with the 10-year yield gap at 105 basis points in early Friday trade. Some analysts said Bunds were set to push this out to 115 basis points in the near term.
By 0655 GMT, the benchmark Bund due August 2007 was trading at 101.99, offering a 5.730 percent yield.
